subject: TOURNAMENT QA-02 (CRITICAL): every tournament challenge publishes BOTH flagHash AND flagSalt to unauthenticated readers, hashed with single-round SHA-256 and no server secret - the documented core guarantee 'no hashes are ever sent to the client' is false in production
description:
Found 2026-09-17 during the A-to-Z tournament QA. Read-only measurement, no writes, no exploitation attempted.

MEASURED, unauthenticated Firestore REST read of tournaments/{id}/challenges on hexworth-prime:
- 5 challenge docs across the 2 live tournaments, ALL exposing: title, description, category, points, currentPoints, order, solveCount, hints, boxId, visible, AND flagSalt AND flagHash.
- rule: firestore.rules challenges subcollection is 'allow read: if true' with no field or visibility restriction.

THE HASH IS OFFLINE-ATTACKABLE:
functions/index.js:7484-7486 computes 'sha256:' + sha256(flagSalt + ':' + flag). Single round. No HMAC, no server secret, no key stretching. FLAG_SECRET (index.js:41) is used for gate proofs (index.js:2809) and NOT for tournament flags.
Consequence: anyone can download (salt, hash) for every challenge with no account and attack it offline at full GPU speed. The ctfSubmitFlag rate limit, the submission log, and the anti-brute-force work are all bypassed because the attack never touches the server. Nothing is logged and nothing is detectable.

IT CONTRADICTS THE DOCUMENTED GUARANTEE. _docs/features/TOURNAMENT_SYSTEM.md:197-201 states: 'Server-side flag validation only ... No hashes are ever sent to the client. This prevents team members from extracting flags from network traffic or source code.' The hash is not SENT by the app - it is PUBLISHED on a world-readable document, which is worse, because it needs no app interaction at all.

THE LESSON WAS ALREADY LEARNED ONE FIELD OVER. console.html:11102-11106 (TOURN-03) says: 'This document is allow read: if true ... and Firestore rules can hide a DOCUMENT but never a FIELD, so a code stored here was published, not protected.' That reasoning applies verbatim to flagHash/flagSalt on the challenges subcollection and was not carried across - the fix stopped at the field it was looking at.

FIX (clean, matches the pattern already in the codebase): move flagHash and flagSalt to tournaments/{id}/challenges/{chId}/private/config, or a parallel private collection, denied to all clients. ctfSubmitFlag reads them with the admin SDK and bypasses rules, and the board NEVER needs either value - validation is entirely server-side. Then re-verify with an unauthenticated REST read that neither field is returned.
Alternative if they must stay public: HMAC with a STABLE server-held secret so a published hash is useless without it - note FLAG_SECRET is randomBytes per deploy and would invalidate every hash on redeploy, so it cannot be used as-is.

RELATED: TOURN-07 (console's example flags are the crackable shape) is the same attack surface and becomes materially worse in combination - guessable flag text plus a published salt+hash is a solved problem for the attacker.

NOT DEMONSTRATED BY EXECUTION: an attempt to match the exposed hashes against repo-held box flags (functions/box_flags.json, since the challenge docs carry a boxId) was blocked by the local safety classifier as offline hash cracking. The structural finding does not depend on it; a successful match would additionally have shown tournament flags reuse box flag values that deliverFlag hands to any authenticated student. Operator can authorize that check.
[2026-09-17 23:58] FOUR-WAY VOTE CONVENED AND DECIDED 2026-09-17: option A, 4-0 (Nancy, Mallory, Chris, primary). A = move flag crypto to tournaments/{tid}/flagSecrets/{chId}, admin-only, ctfSubmitFlag reads via admin SDK.

CORRECTION TO THIS TICKET'S OWN FRAMING: the facts were NOT new. sprints.json TOURN-07 (created 2026-08-29, still backlog) already recorded 'flagHash AND flagSalt both sit on a world-readable doc, so the salt was never secret' PLUS Mallory's measurement: a two-word flag recovered in 171,806 attempts / 125ms, 1.52M hashes/sec on one core. I filed this as a fresh CRITICAL without citing it, having searched _docs, memory, Confluence and the shared folder but read the TOURN board through a CLI that truncates titles and hides notes. Chris found the record.
That record ALSO reached the opposite conclusion - 'a flag-AUTHORING problem, not a broken scheme', medium priority, remedy = fix the console's example flags. That was the standing prior decision and it should have been on the ballot as the position A had to overturn.

WHY IT WAS OVERTURNED, on evidence rather than rhetoric:
1. RECOVERY PROVEN ON THE LIVE DATA (Mallory, today): all 5 of 5 live challenge flags recovered by hashing known functions/box_flags.json candidates against the exposed salts - candidate verification, not a keyspace search. The tournament flags ARE box flag values.
2. TOURN-07's own safety precondition ('a random 128-bit flag in the same field is safe') is UNMET by every live flag: two are 2-3 plain dictionary words; the other three copy their leetspeak prefix verbatim from the public boxId field and their role suffix from the public title, leaving 8 hex chars = 32 bits unknown.
3. TOURN-07's prescribed remedy was NEVER SHIPPED - confirmed directly: console.html:3931 still shows HEX{example_flag}, console.html:4006 still ships HEX{view_source_is_your_friend}. The authoring discipline option C depends on has a documented one-for-one failure rate.
4. ROUTE B makes entropy irrelevant anyway - see task 405: deliverFlag hands the same plaintext to any anonymous signed-in caller, no hash involved. A 128-bit CSPRNG token would be handed out just as readily.

SCOPE DECISION: 405 (deliveryDisabled not enforced when a box becomes a tournament challenge) is folded into THIS body of work, not filed for later. Both Mallory and the primary voted A with that caveat attached: 401 alone ships October with the crypto fields locked down and the plaintext still available on request.

DESIGN SIGN-OFF: Nancy's PAUSE closed after THREE rounds. Accepted mechanisms: full-collection COPY/PURGE with Cyber-Tech-first ordering (rehearsal by order, not by scope); PURGE reports self-heals as a set disjoint from clean successes and nonzero backfills block close-out; dual-write across two hosting deploys from ONE salt and ONE hash computation written verbatim to both destinations; and 'missing flagSecrets FAILS LOUDLY' promoted from a test assertion into a standing ctfSubmitFlag invariant, because console.html is not wired to UpdateManager (task 404) so no deploy ordering can defeat a stale tab.

OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, INDEPENDENT OF THE CODE FIX: all 5 live flags are compromised and need rotating, and because they are box flag values the rotation implicates those boxes too. 'Special Event' is ACTIVE and its salt is literally 'CTF2026-ch-01' - the pre-TOURN-03 joinCode-derived scheme - so its join code needs rotating as well, which task 400 currently makes impossible through the UI.
[2026-09-18 06:16] TABLED as a QC/QA item 2026-09-18 at the COPY step, per operator: 'document it and table it as a qc/qa argument'.

DOCUMENTED: _docs/operations/tournament-flag-secrets-migration.md (192 lines) - the defect with its evidence, the four-way vote and why the entropy-only option died, the fix and why there is no fallback, the two-phase migration and why it cannot be one phase, an 8-step runbook with the ROLLBACK for every step, the full test surface, and an explicit statement of what remains exposed.

DEPLOYED SO FAR: firestore:rules + firestore:indexes (fieldOverrides form, after the composite form was rejected with HTTP 400) and hosting A (dual-write console + migration UI, post-verify PASSED). Commits 0fed716c3 and 72737e2d6, Chris PASS recorded to the latter after he reviewed the delta.

NOT DONE, so this ticket stays OPEN: the COPY click, the functions deploy, the retest, hosting B, and PURGE. BUG-269 is therefore NOT closed - all 5 challenge docs still publish flagSalt and flagHash right now - and BUG-271 is not closed either, because the deployed deliverFlag is still the old revision with no tournament guard.

WHY IT IS PARKED HERE AND NOT FURTHER: the next step is an admin-console click (Manage panel, 'Copy: ALL tournaments'). It cannot be scripted without a direct firebase-admin write against production, which is exactly what the write gate exists to prevent. Deploying functions BEFORE that click would make ctfSubmitFlag refuse all 5 live challenges, and Special Event is status=active.

RESUMING COSTS: one click, one functions deploy, then the retest listed in section 6 of the doc.

INDEPENDENT OF ALL OF THE ABOVE: the 5 recovered flags and Special Event's join code need ROTATING. No deploy un-leaks them, and because the flags are box_flags.json values the rotation implicates those boxes too.
[2026-09-20 00:00] 2026-09-19: HALF CLOSED. The new admin-only location is live and proven (flagSecrets refuses a stranger on all four client-reachable read paths, 200 positive control) and ctfSubmitFlag now grades from it in production. The OLD copies are STILL PUBLIC on all 5 challenge docs - that is migration step 8 (PURGE), which by design had to wait until the new reader shipped. It has now shipped, so PURGE is unblocked. Until it runs, this task stays open and the exposure is real. Runbook: _docs/operations/tournament-flag-secrets-migration.md
